message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"0","derivation":"Retained the source-constructed B(r) with C=0 unchanged from P01_W0. Local verification: the increment is g = r/2 + chi_r*chi_u*(r^2*B), and with B = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2), the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r vanishes identically for all r in the chi_r support (1+r >= 1/2 > 0, so sqrt is C-infinity on an open neighborhood of the evaluation rectangle). The whole residual retains the cross term 2*u*g = O(u*r), which no smooth C(r,u) can cancel: eliminating it would require C ~ 1/u near u=0, violating smoothness. Numerical confirmation from generation-1 feedback: all in-support rows (|r|<=1/2, |u|<=1/4) carry status APPLIED with residuals matching O(u*r) at the expected magnitude (e.g., UNIFORM x=1/8 s=0: |residual|=1.5e-6, |u*r|=0.00778*0.000193=1.5e-6). Rows with |u|>1/4 (LEFT x=1/8 s=0: u=-0.5) or |r|>1/2 correctly fall to g=r/2 with no correction. ZERO family remains exactly z=1.0. No NO_APPLIED_UPDATE failures. Limitations: (1) cancellation is exact only at u=0; the O(ur) cross-term is structural to the two-slot covariance quotient and is not removable by any smooth C. (2) If a future stage drives r below -1 before chi_r fades, sqrt(1+r) hits a negative argument and that specific point records NO_APPLIED_UPDATE (z unchanged); current targets keep r well above -1. (3) No PDE, global, or full-NS claim follows from this local coefficient identity.","inspect":[{"file_id":"CALC/draft.json","limit":2048,"offset":0}],"note":"Successor should verify: (1) After this stage, z_after deviates from 1 by O(tau) at non-ZERO points, so u at the next stage is O(tau) and the residual at the next step is O(tau^2) from the cross-term plus O(tau^2) from the new r shift. (2) The LEFT/RIGHT/BOTH families at t=1/128 show points with z as far as -31 or 17; these have |r|>>1/2 or |u|>>1/4, so chi_r or chi_u is zero and only g=r/2 applies. This is correct and expected; no action needed. (3) C=0 is retained as the source-published choice. A nonzero C would add O(u^2*r) to the residual, which is smaller than the existing O(u*r) and does not improve the leading cross-term. (4) The chi_r support boundary is |r|=1/2; the chi_u boundary is |u|=1/4. The smooth C-infinity transition (same fixed step in both) means the correction fades to zero smoothly; no discontinuity or kink. (5) The archived finite-root expressions (L00_s1_W2, etc.) remain valid for their original finite-task scope; this smooth body is the field-stage operator and does not re-grade those results."}
